USA License Plate Map 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle in the Shape of the US - 31 inches long - Cool Wall Art [[VIDEOID:ece742fa9f80992e2861a156e954114a]] I really like puzzles of maps, and this one is very interesting and unique. It was a pretty easy puzzle to put together, because the license plates from each of the states have a ton of different colors and patterns on them.

Since this is a shaped puzzle, you'll have to rethink how you do puzzles, especially if you put the edge pieces together first. Literally the last piece I put together was an edge piece from California. It's hard to put the edge pieces together, but there are tons of easier parts to put together, so if you're flexible, then it is very doable.

Each state is in the true shape of the state, and it has a license plate or plates instead of any kind of map. There are some vanity plates, like "Elvis Lives" and "Polkatown," but most are regularly-numbered plates.

The puzzle pieces are very average thickness and they're very average quality. They're not great, but they're not bad. But I got this for the shape and the design, so I was very happy overall.

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. I was afraid to force it to completely connect and potentially breaking the plastic connector. It is listed to be for 12-36 months, and up to 40 pounds. Personally, I think 12 months is a little young to be riding this, especially if your child is on the small side and not completely steady on their feet when walking. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad

Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor

These worked great for us, but to be honest, those small pieces get lost pretty quickly. My son usually plays with the ship without those.

My favorite feature is the pegs that are placed ALL over the ship. There are little holes on the bottom of Jake and Skully's feet, so you can place them on the pegs and hold them in place while playing. There's even a little clear bar at the very top of the ship that you can put them on, so it looks like they're flying. I think it's a really cool feature!! I also really like the "rocking" motion of the ship when it moves. It kind of wobbles back and forth to look like it's floating on waves.

My only complaints is the sound, first of all. The music sounds kind of like it's coming from cheap speakers, and I find it annoying. My son loves it and likes to press the buttons to hear the music and phrases. If you really didn't like that feature, the batteries could be taken out. (I haven't resorted to that, but it is an option, since my son knows how to swap the on/off switch). Secondly, I do wish that this set also came with Izzy and Cubby, instead of just Jake and Skully. There are stickers on the side of the boat of Izzy and Cubby to look like they are looking out the window waving. I guess that's an attempt to make up for not having them as figurines. I know that you can buy separate figurines, but I don't know if they have pegs on the bottom of their feet to work with this ship.

Overall, our whole family gives it 2 thumbs up! We all love it, and definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive]

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

Integy RC Model C23347ORANGE Magnetic Parts Storage Tray 88x107mm for Hardware, Screws & Nuts These colorful parts trays have been on my wish list for a number of years. Before I could get one they suddenly seemed to become scarce, and they’re not easy to find these days.

I grabbed this orange one as soon as I saw it being offered, and I’m extremely pleased with it. At 4.2" x 3.5” they are small but that’s my preference. This is for hobby and electronics parts, not for rebuilding an engine. A smaller footprint won’t interfere with a project, and I never liked the bulky chromed 6” types for that reason.

These are offered in a variety of anodized aluminum colors. The orange was the only color available at the time and that’s good because it’s my favorite. If the green becomes available I’ll get that one too, but the colors are so cool I could be happy with just about any of them.

The tray is light and sturdy, comes with a sheet of sized magnetic rubber that has adhesive on the back, plus 4 rubber feet that are also peel and stick.

Integy is a well-known company that manufactures very cool looking parts for the R/C world of cars and planes. You can’t go wrong with anything they make.

Wonder Forge Cat in The Hat I Can Do That! Kids Activity Game This is a fun game that lets little ones simply be silly, while also learning to follow directions. It lets them move around a bit, and "get the sillies out" when that's something that needs to happen.

Within the game, you'll get several props. Some of them are foam, but some are plastic. You'll also get a stack of cards, with numbers 1, 2 or 3 on them. Each player, taking turns, will draw one card of each number, and then follow the directions. For example, card 1 might say "Take four giant steps", card 2 "with the fish", and card 3 "on your head". You'll put the cards together, and the player has to "Take four giant steps with the fish on your head". The combinations will constantly change. My 4 and 6 year old loved it. We tried to include my 2 year old, but he seems to be still a bit young for it.

My boys had fun with it, and it's especially perfect to play after a Dr. Seuss read aloud!

Reading info for Major Arcana cards- general meaning and interpretation (upright), love and relationships (upright), money and career (upright), general meaning and interpretation (reversed), love and relationships (reversed) & money and career (reversed)
Reading info for Minor Arcana cards- general, love, career, reversed general, reversed love & reversed career
I think this will go a long way to helping folks become familiar with the cards rather than viewing a reversed card as strictly an opposite meaning.

Despite its somewhat simple looking art that is pretty faithful to Waite-Rider imagery, there's something very appealing about this deck, for lack of a better term, it feels "open". I know my picture doesn't highlight this, the edges of the cards are gilded as well. I am very pleased with this deck and look forward to having it for a very, very long time.

The older kids help the younger ones trace and color a design using the included pencils. I then take the colored pieces and put them into the oven so harden them up and shrink them. text_fidelity_a:
Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity My grandson is almost three years old, and I thought he’d enjoy this toy...that was until I received it. Upon first inspection you notice a cheaply made zip-up half circle that opens to expose rivets that a child is supposed to insert the enclosed plastic big “buttons”. Let me just tell you that there’s no way that my grandson can attach these things to the mat - it took all my strength and dexterity to get one or two to pop in place. This is simply too difficult for a child of any age and not challenging but frustrating. Then there’s these cute little ocean-themed felt cut-outs that you’re supposed to “hook” around the installed buttons. They’re brightly colored and my grandson did enjoy taking them off and on the buttons for about 15 minutes. Then there’s a few pieces of string...some are about 4” long (too short to practice tying and really too short for a toddler to attempt to thread through four holes on the felt pieces) and others are about 6” long. ALSO, Within fifteen minutes of play my toddler was pulling on the buttons attempting to remove them and the rivets we’re poppong off and the mat was falling apart, not to mention the tiny metal circles all over the floor were now a choking hazard and the mat no longer works in the holes that lost the rivets.

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity

EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments I used to work in Microbiology and one job in particular pertained to streaking for bacteria and viruses on various types of agar plates. We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!
text_fidelity_b: EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments

Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit) The Klutz kits are hit and miss for us, but this one was a hit. Now, that said, like a lot of the Klutz kits, this is a difficult one for children, and will require a very hands on adult helper.

The designs are very nice, and the instructions are good throughout if you have Google or sewing knowledge. It's not that it's going to be terribly difficult to figure out how to sew necessarily, but some of the designs are reasonably complex. I'm not a sewer, but I could figure it out, and instruct my little ones. There are a lot of steps to some of them, and the dexterity needed means that this is going to be one for the older children almost exclusively - they'll need some "advanced" skills like maintaining an even stitch pattern that is not too widely spaced or narrow, figuring out what "whip-stitching" is without it being explained thoroughly, and so forth. Because the designs are all fairly small, you can make one, then save the rest for later, and the kit will see use for many crafting sessions.

I'm very impressed by the finished product as well. Overall, a fun and educational experience for the little ones and for myself as well.
text_fidelity_b: Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit)

2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans This is one of the better kits that this brand makes. They're compatible with LEGO, albeit of a lower quality overall, and this is another of their designs that don't come with minifigs, and which isn't inherently designed for them. You'll make model police vehicles, but your LEGO dudes won't go riding around in them - they simply won't fit.

The other big downside is that you don't get to do the bags in order like you do with LEGO. You kind of have to open them all at once and work from one gigantic pile in the center of the table. It's messy and can lead to quitting, but that's all part of the experience.

They will fit somewhat within the tractor component, which is the largest piece of this set, and by far the most interesting. There are a number of playable aspects to this that give you a lot more bang for your buck than the more model-focused kits we've tried from Wishalife previously.

Overall, there's plenty of bricks, OK instructions, a large number of stickers, and plenty of fun to be had here. No, it's not LEGO, but it's not too bad considering. This is a great buy to keep your kids playing for some time.

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf Super Soaker Zipfire 3-Pack(Discontinued by manufacturer) UPDATE: Man, these things get the job done! It only took a few reminders, but now the dogs are not barking, either inside or when we go out (even if I don't have a squirt gun with me). All I have to do is pick one up and they immediately run off and cower QUIETLY in the bedroom! I think what makes these work better than dog whistles or scolding or time outs is that they can be targeted at the instigator, not both dogs. So if one dog is quiet, he doesn't get shot; just the offender gets blasted. They figured it out really quickly. They do NOT like to be blasted! LOL! And I think they actually compete to see which one can stay the quietest.

Got these to blast the dogs when they won't stop barking. They don't blast a targeted enough stream unless you are standing closer to the dog, like maybe six feet away, but they seem to work for their intended purpose. The chiweenie Bingo's the really rotten one, and the first time I used one of these pistols, I shot him once, he turned around and defiantly barked at me; I shot him again, same thing; then I shot him in the face with it, and he ran off into another room and stopped barking. The first time I used it with Doobie, a Jack Chi, he responded right away. (These dogs hate getting wet...but a dog who loves water would react differently. Still might quit barking, though.) So I'm hopeful these are going to get the job done. Only time will tell, but so far they see the brightly colored gun in my hand and quit barking.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf Super Soaker Zipfire 3-Pack(Discontinued by manufacturer)
